policy_memory: 128 FIFO original public SHA-256 keys + 6 uint32 per key, 18 global uint32, RNG state and pending key per policy, same fixed allocation budget
isolation: fresh dedicated Python process per policy, sequential execution with no overlapping source-native actors, subprocess stdout/stderr recorded, all original env and evaluator included in process CPU and OS peak resident bytes
resource_measurement: time.process_time_ns for entire worker from start through trace serialization (excluding minor final JSON receipt print); OS ru_maxrss linux / peak_wset Windows; exact process output diagnostic pickle bytes; no allocation omitted from worker
cost_nonregression_strict: same original source-family/seed/stream cohort, source-native action counts and fully separated worker processes. Candidate total CPU <= baseline total CPU AND native source process peak RSS <= baseline. Different source trajectories can have different native step lengths, so report per-step and equal-prefix metrics but do not claim matched execution-workload proof.
causal_coverage_gate: candidate must yield strictly more independent DoorKey reset seed clusters with true same FULL current MR15+action/pose/inventory but different world and next eight-bit consequence than baseline, using only the min actual native episode lengths per matched policy/seed/stream pair
door_gate: candidate visible genuine original key-to-door episodes >= baseline (full native trajectories) and report door-specific strict pairs separately
reproduction: identical original source event digests per platform, clean original worktrees, no synthetic histories, no private grid/pose/inventory to actor
fail_closed_on: nonreproduced Windows vs Linux source receipt
known_limit: isolated process includes native source+posthoc evaluator and trace serialization, but not the parent CI runner/GitHub machine total energy, and policy actions change source workload; per-step CPU isn't algorithm-only cost. Experimental development data only.
